data.body:
MEASURED AUDIT before implementation — the gap is TEN methods, not one. This materially widens the
story, so recording it now rather than discovering it mid-flight.

I ran an AST audit over src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/*.py collecting every method invoked on a
'client' or 'transport' receiver, then diffed that set against JiraDataCenterTransport's methods and
against every Protocol declared in _backend.py.

CALLED BY THE CORE, ABSENT FROM THE DC TRANSPORT (10):
    delete_issue, get_comments, get_issue_by_rest, get_issue_links, get_parent_map,
    remove_label, set_entity_property, set_issue_property, set_reporter, validate_assignee_exists

DECLARED ON NO PROTOCOL IN _backend.py — the SAME 10.

All ten ARE implemented for Cloud, spread across adapters/jira/acli_rest.py, acli.py and
acli_graph.py. (My first pass reported three of them as missing from Cloud too; that was wrong — I
had not scanned acli_graph.py. Corrected before recording: Cloud has all ten.)

WHAT THIS MEANS: set_entity_property is not 'the' missing method, it is simply the FIRST one a live
writing pass happened to reach. Nine more sit behind it. Implementing only set_entity_property would
move the crash one call deeper and produce another red CI run — the story would look like progress
while the capability stayed broken.

The TicketTransport Protocol declares six members (create_issue, get_issue, update_issue,
transition_issue_by_name, add_label, search_issues). The core actually calls fifteen. So the port
describes 40% of its own requirement, which is exactly why isinstance conformance, the backend
contract suite, and 1636 reconciler unit tests were all green against a transport that cannot
complete a writing pass.

IMPLICATION FOR THIS STORY'S SHAPE, for the reviewer: the third AC (the structural audit test) is now
the load-bearing one, not a nicety — it is what converts 'I found ten' into 'the eleventh cannot be
introduced silently'. And the live tests are the only oracle that can confirm the set is actually
complete, since the audit proves what the core calls STATICALLY and cannot prove which paths a real
pass exercises.

Some of the ten may be reachable only on paths a DC deployment never takes; that is a judgement to
make per method WITH evidence, not an assumption. Whatever is deliberately left unimplemented should
raise a clear NotImplementedError naming the DC limitation rather than AttributeError mid-pass.
